# Research Report — 2026-07-16T00:11:58Z

**Links analyzed:** 4
**Relevance breakdown:** 1 high, 2 medium, 1 low (re-scored — see Arc-alignment)

---

## TL;DR

- BIP-110 is a proposed Bitcoin soft fork (championed in the Bitcoin Knots orbit) to restrict data-carrier usage — Ordinals/inscriptions, oversized `OP_RETURN`, BRC-20 — at the consensus layer. It is the counter-move to Bitcoin Core v30 removing the default `OP_RETURN` datacarrier size cap.
- Miner activation signaling **failed**: ~0.7–1.18% of blocks signaled, far below any activation threshold, as of block **958,109**. Michael Saylor branded it the "Bitcoin **I**atrogenic Proposal" (BIP → iatrogenic: harm caused by the treatment itself).
- This is a live Bitcoin protocol-governance fight, not a technical curiosity. It bears directly on whether on-chain data-carrying (which Arc *does* via inscription commit/reveal) stays permissionless.

## Key Takeaways

- **@saylor** ("BIP 110: Bitcoin **I**atrogenic Proposal", ~likes signal high reach) frames restriction as self-inflicted harm to Bitcoin — the pro-datacarrier / anti-filtering position. Source: https://twitter.com/saylor/status/2077297913382748160
- **@CunyRenaud** (bio: "BIP-110 tracking & spam analysis") replies that **Core v30 was the iatrogenic and highly contentious change** — i.e. the restriction camp reads causation the opposite way: removing the OP_RETURN limit was the harm, BIP-110 is the correction. 227 likes / 2,369 impressions. Source: https://x.com/i/status/2077339271489372358
- **@stephanlivera**: "you're just bringing up unrelated FUD because of how unpopular BIP110 is. It's transparent for anyone to see." — reads the failed signaling as a clean market verdict against BIP-110. Source: https://x.com/i/status/2077259415661711865
- **Citadel21 "The Network" (hodlonaut, Mar 2026)** — Article 1 of 4 investigating how informal power over Bitcoin Core "was assembled, exercised, and defended." Documents Bitcoin **Knots** (Luke Dashjr's implementation) surging from ~2% to >20% of the network in months during the autumn-2025 filter fight. This is the governance backdrop that produced BIP-110. Source: https://www.citadel21.com/the-network

## Arc-alignment

**Direct code hook — this is not tangential.** Arc inscribes content onto Bitcoin L1 via `skills/daily-brief-inscribe`, whose lifecycle is `commit-tx` → `reveal-tx` (the Ordinals inscription-envelope pattern: data in Taproot witness). That is precisely the data class BIP-110 / Knots datacarrier filters target. A successful data-carrier soft fork would directly threaten the viability of Arc's inscription skill — cheaper-to-relay today, potentially unminable under a restrictive regime. Arc also tracks the demand side via `skills/ordinals-market-data` and `skills/ordinals-marketplace`.

Second-order: Stacks (Arc's L2) anchors state to Bitcoin L1; a tightening of what L1 will carry is a standing risk to any L2 that leans on Bitcoin data availability. Worth a watch-item, not an action today — signaling failed, so no near-term consensus change.

**Recommendation** (effort: low / impact: medium / risk: low / target: arc-starter):
- No code change. Add BIP-110 / datacarrier-filter status to whatever governance-watch cadence exists; re-open if a re-signaling attempt clears single digits.
- Content angle: the Core-v30-OP_RETURN + BIP-110 pair is a strong candidate for a single packaged "$9 data-carrier war" reader (see `sku_why`). Route via the research→SKU pipeline, not a standalone thin report.
